Article Title: Xi Jinping arrives in Delhi for Brics summit, set for talks with PM Modi
Article Text:
Xi was received at the Delhi airport by Union Minister of State for Commerce and Industry Jitin Prasada

PM Modi-Xi talks amid efforts to repair ties

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived in New Delhi on Saturday for the 18th BRICS Summit , beginning a two-day visit to India that marks his first trip to the country in seven years.Xi was received at the Delhi airport by Union minister of state for commerce and industry Jitin Prasada, with cultural artistes from the Northeast and other parts of India performing traditional dances to welcome the Chinese leader. The ministry of external affairs said on X, “Warm welcome to President Xi Jinping of the People’s Republic of China on his arrival in New Delhi to attend the 18th BRICS Summit. He was received by MoS @JitinPrasada at the airport. We look forward to constructive discussions as BRICS continues to advance cooperation and contribute to a more balanced, representative and multipolar world.”Xi's arrival comes ahead of his bilateral meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, scheduled for 6pm on Saturday.The visit follows a series of high-level engagements between India and China aimed at rebuilding ties after the deadly Galwan Valley clashes in 2020 and the subsequent military standoff in eastern Ladakh.National Security Adviser Ajit Doval held Special Representative talks with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Beijing last month. The discussions covered the India-China boundary question, including delimitation of the frontier, trans-boundary cooperation and maintaining peace along the LAC.Both Doval and Wang are designated Special Representatives for the boundary talks mechanism, established in 2003 to address the 3,488-km India-China border dispute. PM Modi and Xi had also held wide-ranging talks on August 31 last year on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Tianjin.Xi's delegation includes Cai Qi, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and director of the General Office of the CPC Central Committee, as well as Wang Yi, a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Chinese foreign minister.
Article Summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived in New Delhi on Saturday for the 18th BRICS Summit. Xi's arrival comes ahead of his bilateral meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, scheduled for 6pm on Saturday. Visit follows a series of high- level engagements between India and China aimed at rebuilding ties after the deadly Galwan Valley clashes in 2020 and the subsequent military standoff in eastern Ladakh.

Article Title: "Legacy of our ancestors...": CM Pushkar Singh Dhami hails Rudrapur's transformative growth at Punjabi Gaurav Sammelan
Article Text:
"Legacy of our ancestors...": CM Pushkar Singh Dhami hails Rudrapur's transformative growth at Punjabi Gaurav Sammelan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Thursday lauded the pioneering legacy and transformative contributions of the ancestors and various communities in turning Rudrapur into a vibrant industrial hub and the granary of the nation.Speaking at the Punjabi Gaurav Sammelan in Rudrapur, the chief minister expressed deep gratitude to the Sikh Gurus for the ancestral sacrifices that laid the groundwork for the state's progress."I bow in reverence at the feet of all our Gurus. I pray to the Guru Sahibs that the spirit of service towards our society and our state remains alive within all of us," he said.CM Dhami hailed the development done in Rudrapur, highlighting that this is the same region that once faced threats of venomous snakes and scorpions and deadly animals like crocodiles and tigers."Look at the wonderful work being done here; may we all continue to receive the strength to undertake such noble tasks. Every community is progressing. There was a time when people spoke of the dangers here: snakes, scorpions, massive crocodiles, tigers. Yet, it was settled and transformed into what it is today, a hub of industry and a land of lush green fields that serve as a granary, supplying food to the entire nation.This is the legacy of our ancestors; we must cherish and preserve it," he said.Meanwhile, Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) national president Nitin Nabin, who was also present at the programme as part of his two-day visit to the State, highlighted the Centre's interventions to protect persecuted minority communities from neighbouring nations, specifically referencing the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA).Nabin said, "We all know how there was a threat to the existence of the Sikh community in Afghanistan. A law that should have been made in the initial years of independence took a long time to be formed."Further, Nabin emphasised that the Modi government fulfilled a long-standing post-independence commitment by offering refuge and dignity to persecuted Sikhs and Hindus."With CAA (Citizenship Amendment Act), PM Narendra Modi fulfilled the promise that was made to people at the time of independence. Sikhs and Hindus who were facing atrocities in Pakistan, Afghanistan and Bangladesh are welcomed here not as refugees but as the children of this soil," he said.Earlier today, Nitin Nabin and Pushkar Singh Dhami paid floral tributes at the Shaheed Smarak in Haldwin honour of soldiers who laid down their lives for the nation.Nabin, along with CM Dhami, also offered prayers and performed rituals at the Mahalaxmi Temple in Haldwani earlier in the day. (ANI)
Article Summary: Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Thursday lauded the pioneering legacy and transformative contributions of the ancestors and various communities. He expressed deep gratitude to the Sikh Gurus for the ancestral sacrifices that laid the groundwork for the state's progress. Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) national president Nitin Nabin highlighted the Centre's interventions to protect persecuted minority communities.

Article Title: 'Prioritise national interest': Shashi Tharoor advises govt to keep Brics 'non-West'
Article Text:
Shashi Tharoor says govt must keep Brics non-West and not let it appear anti-West.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Shashi Tharoor on Friday cautioned that the Brics summit hosted by India should not appear to be an anti-West platform, as that would not be in sync with the country’s national interests.Tharoor, who served as a diplomat at the United Nations for decades, advised the government to showcase the concerns of the Global South while keeping India’s direct national interests in mind."As chair, we have a particular responsibility to showcase both the Brics as a forum, the concerns of the Global South in general, but also while bearing very, very carefully in mind our direct national interests. We want Brics to be a forum that is non-West, but not anti-West. That is exactly actually the same agenda as every other country. There are some others in Brics who are very happy to take it as a geopolitical non-Western, but also anti-Western platform," Tharoor told news agency PTI.He also said that PM Modi's scheduled meeting with Chinese president Xi Jinping and the meeting with Russian president Vladimir Putin "are going to grab world headlines"."And I would like to say that that would not be in India's national interest...Becauseall these world leaders are in India, there will be significant bilateral conversations. Our Prime Minister is bound to be meeting each of the visiting heads of state and government who seeks a meeting. And that may mean a dozen important meetings with these country leaders. And for us, of course, both the meeting with President Xi and the meeting with President Putin are going to grab world headlines," the Thiruvananthapuram Lok Sabha MP said.Former Union minister Salman Khurshid also described the gathering as a “significant event” that allows India to demonstrate leadership on the global stage.Speaking to ANI, Khurshid stressed that the presence of leaders from all 11 member countries, including China, Iran, Russia, South Africa and India, could help New Delhi bring countries together, reduce contradictions and conflicts, and work towards creating better conditions in the world."This is a significant event. We hosted the G20 summit a few years ago, and the important thing is that the top leadership of China, Iran, Russia, South Africa, and India will all be present. All 11 countries will be present. It allows India to demonstrate leadership and ensure that contradictions and conflicts are reduced to a minimum. It can't be done overnight, but at least some attempt should be made. For India to have a locus as the leader and chairperson of the Brics summit, to be able to bring people together, converge, and accept positions that will create better conditions in the world," he said.Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday said leaders from across the world would gather in New Delhi over the next few days for the Brics summit, expressing confidence that the high-level meeting would see positive and meaningful discussions on various issues with the welfare of the world in mind.“Over the next few days, leaders from around the world will gather for the Brics Summit. I am confident that the Summit will see positive and meaningful discussions on various issues with the welfare of the world in mind,” Modi said in a post on X in Hindi.The Prime Minister also shared a Sanskrit shlok highlighting the importance of cultivating relationships with virtuous people and promoting dialogue and goodwill.“A person should always live among the virtuous and cultivate their company. A person should engage in discussion and foster friendly relations with the virtuous, because mutual goodwill, dialogue and friendly relations strengthen peace and cooperation,” the verse said in a loose translation.As Brics chair in 2026, India will host the 18th Brics summit in New Delhi on September 12 and 13. The summit will bring together leaders of Brics member and partner countries, as well as outreach invitees.During the summit, leaders are expected to discuss ways to strengthen intra-Brics cooperation on common priorities and exchange views on global and regional issues of mutual importance, according to a statement issued by the Ministry of External Affairs.Earlier on Thursday night, Bharat Mandapam, the venue for the summit in New Delhi, was being readied to host the high-profile gathering, with leaders and representatives from across the world expected to arrive for the September 12-13 event.
Article Summary: Shashi Tharoor says govt must keep Brics non-West and not let it appear anti- West. PM Modi's scheduled meeting with Chinese president Xi Jinping and the meeting with Russian president Vladimir Putin "are going to grab world headlines"

Article Title: Guarding Xi: Inside heightened security deployment
Article Text:
This will be Xi Jinping's first India visit since 2019

NEW DELHI: From establishing temporary no-fly zones over his hotel to conducting checks for potential so-called CBRN (Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear) threats, President Xi Jinping’s security during his 24-hour visit to India is expected to reach an unprecedented scale.The security measures are attributed mainly to the perceived threat from a lone-wolf attack or even demonstrations by Tibetan activists. Beijing has warned specifically about the possible use of drones, banners, loudspeakers and balloons as tools for anti-China propaganda and sought effective measures to keep out low-altitude, small-size aerial objects and other UAVs.Xi will land in Delhi around noon on Saturday, accompanied by a 67-member govt entourage comprising senior political figures, diplomats, security officials and medical staff.“All security concerns and issues raised by foreign govts are being addressed as per MEA (ministry of external affairs) protocol in coordination with Delhi Police and other agencies,” said an official source requesting anonymity.Ten days before the visit, China flew in a planeload of cargo items including Xi’s car, Hongqi (red flag) state limousine, another backup car and communication equipment. India allows foreign delegations to carry their own communication equipment, subject to approval by department of telecommunications.Satellite communication equipment is not allowed.In the case of guns and ammunitions, while pistols are allowed, items like sub machine guns and anti-drone equipment cannot be imported and must be left with customs at the airport on arrival.Apart from attending a Brics summit session on Saturday, Xi will have a bilateral meeting with PM Narendra Modi and join him later for a state dinner. Indian authorities have been requested by the Chinese to allow Xi’s staff to access the kitchen, apparently to sample some of the dishes on the menu and ensure they conform to the president’s dietary preferences. Like with the millet-heavy G20 menu, food on this occasion too is likely to be vegetarian.Apart from deployment of counter-terrosism forces and anti-explosion devices, the president’s hotel will also undergo comprehensive anti-nuclear, anti-radiation and anti-biochemical security checks ahead of his arrival. Security measures also include an inspection of the underground pipeline networks. Xi will be in India for 24 hours and will depart for the airport from Bharat Mandapam around 11 am on Sunday.
Article Summary: Xi Jinping's security during his 24-hour visit to India is expected to reach an unprecedented scale. Beijing has warned specifically about the possible use of drones, banners, loudspeakers and balloons as tools for anti-China propaganda. Xi will land in Delhi around noon on Saturday, accompanied by a 67-member entourage.

Article Title: Shashi Tharoor answers Chidambaram’s questions on Brics benefits for India; BJP takes digs
Article Text:
It's Congress vs Congress again, this time over Brics Summit that is being held in Delhi.

Tharoor joins debate

Tharoor vs Congress

NEW DELHI: Shashi Tharoor not being in sync with his Congress colleagues is no longer news. Especially, if the issue in question pertains to the global stage. So, when senior Congress leader Chidambaram questioned the benefits of Brics for India, Tharoor had an answer. As expected, the answer triggered another round of Tharoor vs Congress debate that overshadowed the BJP broadside against Chidambaram.On Wednesday, Chidambaram questioned the tangible benefits India has gained from recent Brics summits, and said he had not seen any significant outcomes from the last two or three meetings.“I don't know how many presidents and how many prime ministers are coming. I don't think the last two or three Brics summits have resulted in tangible benefits or tangible results,” Chidambaram stated. “In fact, we are part of Brics, we are part of SCO, we are part of G20, and we are part of QUAD. What benefits are we getting out of that? I can't see. In the last two or three summits, I didn't see any benefits. Earlier, the Brics summits resulted in some tangible benefits,” he added.Chidambaram’s remarks opened the floodgates for counter-attacks from the ruling party. The BJP leaders launched a broadside against Chidambaram and the Congress. What followed was a barrage of attacks ranging from "Dimagi Naxal", "Naraz Fufas in pain", "FOMO", "indigestion", "bitten by bug" to questions on what Congress had gained in diplomacy since Independence"Is diplomacy to be seen as a transaction like the Congress Party is projecting? What have I done for you? What will you do for me? Kind of an approach.What is the so-called tangible result?" BJP leader Nalin Kohli wondered.Kohli then questioned the Congress party's own diplomatic record from Independence until 2014. "If we talk of tangible results, we can question what the Congress Party's entire approach from 1947 right up to 2014 was on diplomacy, including Sharm El Sheikh and projecting Pakistan as literally a victim of terror when it is the perpetrator of terror," he stated.Tharoor then joined the debate and said India holding Brics was a matter of prestige. "Having a dozen heads of state and government, not only members of Brics but also some observers coming at presidential and prime ministerial level, is a matter of great prestige for us. It shows a certain diplomatic convening power, which has value in and of itself on the global stage," Tharoor said.The Congress MP maintained that the Brics Summit is providing an important platform for the Global South."This grouping, the 11 Brics countries, represents a majority of the world's population and 41 per cent of global GDP. It's not a small matter; it's something that has to be taken very seriously by the rest of the world. Secondly, of course, having a dozen heads of state and government, not only members of BRICS but also some observers coming at the presidential and prime ministerial level, this is a matter of great prestige for us," the Congress MP from Thiruvananthapuram said.Latching onto Tharoor’s remarks, Nalin Kohli said: “One has noted Dr Shashi Tharoor's statement, and anyone who understands diplomacy would see great value in the BRICS summit.”BJP leader Pradeep Bhandari also used Tharoor’s remarks to take digs at the Congress and allege that some party leaders were opposing Brics on the instructions of Rahul Gandhi “Congress exposes Congress! Congress MP Shashi Tharoor says-" BRICS happening in India is a matter of huge prestige for Bharat." Congress MP exposes "Naraz Fufa" of Congress who were opposing BRICS on instructions of Rahul Gandhi!” Pradeep Bhandari said in a post on X.Tharoor has had frosty ties with the Congress over his “independent views” on a range of issues. In the last two years, Tharoor has often made the Congress duck for cover as the BJP has cited his views to school the grand-old-party. The Thiruvananthapuram MP has made several remarks over a wide range of issues - from lessons in nationalism to global diplomacy to the Emergency to Covid-19 vaccine distribution abroad - that have brought more cheers to the BJP than his own party, the Congress.It all started with Tharoor's surprise "out-of-turn" praise for Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s US trip after Donald Trump took oath as president for a second term.Tharoor then acknowledged key achievements from PM Modi’s visit, particularly on trade negotiations and defence cooperation. He welcomed the trade deal discussions and expressed optimism over India’s diplomatic engagements.The Congress immediately issued a clarification, which said that individual opinions do not reflect the party’s official stance. But Tharoor defended his remarks and said: “When someone in the government does the right thing, it should be recognised, irrespective of who's in power. For 16 years, I have been in politics. My attitude has been that when somebody in the government, whether it’s our government or some other party’s government, does the right thing or does something well, one should acknowledge and praise it, and when they do something badly, one should criticise it. If I were to praise all the time, no one would take me seriously. If I were to criticise all the time, no one would take me seriously either… There’s got to be some give and take in democracy.”After the Pahalgam terror attack and Centre's Operation Sindoor, Tharoor made several remarks that were at variance with the official stand taken by the Congress.Tharoor was picked up to lead a multi-party parliamentary delegation to represent India globally following Operation Sindoor. Later, writing for The Hindu, Tharoor praised Modi’s "energy, dynamism, and willingness to engage" as a major asset for India on the global stage. He described Modi’s multi-alignment strategy as a key pillar in projecting India's voice globally.At one stage, Tharoor said Modi’s foreign policy was remarkable as the Prime Minister was maintaining excellent relations with Russia while simultaneously pursuing strategic relations with the USA. Modi has raised Bharat as a powerful and independent force and has put forward a policy of “multi-alignment”.In May last year, during the inauguration of the Vizhinjam International Seaport in Thiruvananthapuram, Prime Minister Modi acknowledged the presence of Tharoor on stage and remarked that it would give "sleepless nights" to many in the opposition INDIA bloc.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi held a meeting with Tharoor in January this year ahead of assembly elections in Kerala and tried to sort out the differences and project a unified picture.Tharoor has all along defended his remarks and has claimed that his stand on several international issues was "pro-India, and not pro-BJP," stressing that national interest transcends party lines.Clearly, for Shashi Tharoor, his remarks on Brics are par for the course. It is the Congress that has to decide - how to handle the independent views of its MP from Thiruvananthapuram.
Article Summary: Congress leader Chidambaram questioned the benefits of Brics for India. Tharoor said India holding Brics was a matter of prestige for the country. BJP leaders launched a broadside against the ruling party and the Congress. The Congress MP from Thiruvananthapuram has made several remarks over a range of issues.

Article Title: PM gifts Putin Russian version of Tamil text 'Thirukkural'
Article Text: NEW DELHI: A Russian translation of 'Thirukkural', the influential Tamil work whose wisdom PM Narendra Modi has often drawn on in his speeches, was his gift to Russian President Vladimir Putin Friday as they met ahead of the Brics summit.The ancient book carries 1,330 short couplets offering moral guidance on principally three pursuits - virtue, govt and society, and love. Besides Modi, parliamentarians, especially those from Tamil Nadu, often quote from it. Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman has drawn from it during her budget speeches and so has P Chidambaram when he was in office.While the book offers wisdom on the strategy for war when needed, it also emphasises the virtue of peace - a principle Modi has often advocated by stressing the need to avoid conflicts. In their past meetings, he has nudged Putin to end the Ukraine conflict, which is now in its fifth year."Presented President Putin with a Russian translation of the Thirukkural, which carries the eternal wisdom of the great Thiruvalluvar across languages and borders," Modi said.
Article Summary: The ancient book carries 1,330 short couplets offering moral guidance on principally three pursuits - virtue, govt and society, and love. The book offers wisdom on the strategy for war when needed, it also emphasises the virtue of peace - a principle Modi has often advocated.

Article Title: Tharoor: Hosting Brics matter of 'great prestige'
Article Text:
Shashi Tharoor on Brics

NEW DELHI: A day after Congress's P Chidambaram said the last 2-3 Brics summits have been without any tangible benefits for the country, party MP Shashi Tharoor Friday said it is par for course in diplomacy and one values a platform because it demonstrates India's influence to convene meetings of important countries.Chidambaram said Brics used to deliver concrete benefits but has stopped doing so, in what appeared a way of comparing the summits during Congress's tenure with that under BJP govt. Tharoor conceded his point, adding the last time there was a tangible benefit was when he, as UPA finance minister, saw the launch of "development bank" in Brics."We have been longer on lofty rhetoric and grand declarations but shorter on tangible measurable outcomes. But that is par for course in diplomacy...," he said. "Having a dozen heads of state and govt... is a matter of great prestige." TNN
Article Summary: Party MP Shashi Tharoor said it is par for course in diplomacy. He said one values a platform because it demonstrates India's influence. Chidambaram said Brics used to deliver concrete benefits but has stopped doing so. He appeared to be comparing summits during Congress's tenure with that under BJP govt.

JAMMU: Udhampur district administration Thursday imposed a two-month prohibition on all Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), citing security concerns over their alleged use to circumvent lawful cyber restrictions. “The directive was issued on Sept 10 under BNSS Section 163 and came into force with immediate effect. The order will remain applicable for two months unless rescinded, amended, or withdrawn earlier,” an official said.Earlier, Doda district administration had issued a similar two-month VPN ban order on Sept 7.According to the directive issued by Udhampur district magistrate, inputs from security and intelligence agencies suggested that certain individuals and groups were using VPNs to evade cyber restrictions and access prohibited websites, applications and digital platforms.Such misuse could threaten public order, peace, and security, and could facilitate unlawful, anti-national, and disruptive activities such as circulating inflammatory/objectionable content, inciting violence or unrest, and coordinating illegal acts, the order stated.The restriction extends to individuals, institutions, cyber cafés, commercial establishments and internet service providers operating in Udhampur. VPN services may be used only when authorised by govt/competent authority through an official order. Violations will attract legal action, the directive warned.

SRINAGAR: Hurriyat Conference chairman Mirwaiz Umar Farooq left for New Delhi on Friday to attend an interaction with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian.In a statement issued here, Mirwaiz said following the invitation of the Iranian ambassador to India, he will be attending an interaction with President Pezeshkian, who is in the capital to attend the BRICS Summit.“The interaction of religious leaders, intellectuals and other dignitaries, is being hosted by Iran’s ambassador to India, Dr Mohammad Fathali, which is scheduled to take place in New Delhi later Friday followed by a dinner reception,” the statement said.In March this year, Mirwaiz, Kashmir’s chief cleric, had led a delegation of Kashmiri religious leaders to meet Dr Fathali at the Iranian embassy in New Delhi, where they expressed condolences over the killing of Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, his family members and others and expressed “deep solidarity with the people of Iran.During the meeting, Mirwaiz had highlighted the “deep-rooted cultural, historical and religious ties between Kashmir and Iran,” stating that Kashmir has long been referred to as “Iran-e-Sagheer” (little Iran).After the killing of Khamenei, thousands of people in Kashmir gathered in Srinagar’s Lal Chowk and later in Budgam, with crowds stretching several kilometres, to mourn his death. Article Title: No vaccine-autism link, finds WHO review
Article Text:
WHO found no causal link between vaccines and autism after reviewing studies from 2010 to August 2025.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: At a time when the debate has resurfaced in the United States, a 15-year review by the World Health Organization (WHO) has reaffirmed that there is no causal link between vaccines and autism. The findings not only dismantle persistent myths but also underscore the safety of vaccines, reinforcing the critical role immunisation plays in public health worldwide.Autism spectrum disorder is a group of neurodevelopmental conditions that can affect social interaction and communication skills, with signs typically emerging in early childhood.The controversy began in 1998, when a study led by British doctor Andrew Wakefield claimed that the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine could be linked to autism. The study was later retracted byThe Lancet, but the claim continued to spread.The issue gained fresh attention in the US on Aug 10, when President Donald Trump signed an executive order seeking changes to childhood vaccine recommendations and raised the issue of autism during the signing ceremony. Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr, who has long questioned vaccine safety, backed the move. However, WHO’s Global Advisory Committee on Vaccine Safety has repeatedly examined the issue and found no evidence of a causal relationship.The findings are particularly relevant for India, where measles-rubella vaccination is part of the national immunisation programme, with the govt working towards measles-rubella elimination by 2026. The Union health ministry launched the National Zero Measles-Rubella Elimination Campaign 2025-26 in April 2025, with children up to five years targeted for two doses of the vaccine. Its 2025-26 annual report puts first-dose coverage at 98.6% for April-Dec 2025.The WHO review, published on Sept 3, assessed peer-reviewed studies from 2010 to Aug 2025. It included 31 primary studies and five meta-analyses, along with 21 narrative reviews. Methodologically the most rigorous studies did not support a causal association between vaccines, including those containing thiomersal, and autism spectrum disorder.Studies reporting a positive association were rated as having very low strength of evidence and high risk of bias, while none of the meta-analyses supported a causal link. The review also found no convincing evidence that thiomersal, an organomercury preservative, causes autism. WHO said the overall evidence supports the safety of current vaccines.WHO also cautioned that the rise in autism diagnoses should not automatically be attributed to vaccination. Improved identification, broader diagnostic criteria and greater awareness could be contributing to higher diagnosis rates.
Article Summary: 15-year review by the World Health Organization has reaffirmed that there is no causal link between vaccines and autism. The controversy began in 1998, when a study led by British doctor Andrew Wakefield claimed that the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine could be linked to autism.

Article Title: JD(U) renaming on cards? Leaders back proposal to name party after Nitish

JDU leader Nitish Kumar. Photo credit: ANI

NEW DELHI: The Janata Dal (United) is considering a proposal to rename the more than two-decade-old party as ‘JD(U)-Nitish’, in recognition of its supreme leader and former Bihar chief minister Nitish Kumar The suggestion was made by JD(U) working president Sanjay Kumar Jha, who was heard in a purportedly recorded video saying the party owed its standing to Kumar and that its ideology was rooted in his political philosophy.“We should therefore consider renaming the party as JD(U)-Nitish,” Jha was heard saying.The proposal has received backing from senior JD(U) leaders, including Bihar deputy chief minister Bijendra Prasad Yadav and minister Shrawon Kumar.Yadav, a former state president of the JD(U), said, “It is a very good suggestion. Let there be a formal discussion on the matter so that a decision could be taken.”Shrawon Kumar said, “There could not have been a better proposal. I suggest that a formal resolution be brought by the party at the earliest. It is bound to be passed unanimously.”The JD(U) was formed in 2003 through the merger of the Sharad Yadav-led Janata Dal and the Samata Party.Though Sharad Yadav served as its national president until 2016, Nitish Kumar was widely regarded as its de facto leader. Kumar formally took over as national president in 2016.The development comes days after Jha rejected a separate proposal to rename Bakhtiyarpur, Kumar’s birthplace, as ‘Nitishpur’ on Thursday. Responding to the suggestion by Hindustani Awam Morcha national president Santosh Kumar Suman, Jha said Kumar “has always let his work speak on his behalf” and “has never believed in renaming places”.Jha also said, “Let us bear in mind that merely changing the name of the place will not erase from history the fact that Bakhtiyar Khilji had invaded the land and set Nalanda, the ancient seat of learning, on fire”.The proposal to rename the town had also drawn support from Union minister Chirag Paswan. “This is indeed a good suggestion. Nitish Kumar ji has contributed immensely to the progress of Bihar over a long period of time,” Paswan said.The RJD, meanwhile, has criticised both proposals. RJD MLA Bhai Virendra claimed the party could split within months, alleging that the developments pointed in that direction.The JD(U) is yet to announce any formal decision on renaming the party.
Article Summary: Janata Dal (United) is considering a proposal to rename the more than two- decade-old party as ‘JD(U)-Nitish’, in recognition of its supreme leader and former Bihar chief minister Nitish Kumar. The proposal has received backing from senior JD(U) leaders, including Bihar deputy chief minister Bijendra Prasad Yadav.

Article Title: ‘Why is government silent?’ Congress targets BJP over US ‘Mr Singh’ ad
Article Text:
Jairam Ramesh said the ad was not merely an insult to an individual or community but to 'the dignity of all Indians'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Congress on Friday attacked the government over a controversial US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) advertisement targeting “Mr Singh”. The opposition called it an insult to all Indians and questioned why New Delhi had not issued a strong public rebuttal. The opposition party accused the government of being “weak” and failing to firmly defend India’s interests and the dignity of Indians abroad.Congress general secretary in-charge communications Jairam Ramesh said the advertisement, which used AI-generated imagery of a brown-bearded, turbaned man with messages including “Get off our roads, you don't know how to drive Mr Singh” and “Self-deport or find out”, was highly offensive.“Modi ji, who has been showcasing his international clout by calling Donald Trump his 'friend' and who even coined the slogan 'Abki Baar Trump Sarkar' among Indian-Americans, is now seeing continuous insults against Indians and people of Indian origin under his administration,” Ramesh said.“Yet, the Modi government is behaving as if it is a silent partner in this entire episode. An extremely offensive poster targeting 'Mr Singh' was issued from the official handle of the US Department of Homeland Security, in which a turbaned Indian was threatened with lines like 'Get off our roads' and 'Self-deport or find out',” he said in a post in Hindi on X.Ramesh said the episode was not merely an insult to an individual or community but to “the dignity of all Indians”. He said the government should have strongly rebutted what he described as racial stereotyping and “this level of governmental rudeness”.The DHS later removed the advertisement following protests in the US, Ramesh said. However, he alleged that the department continued to defend the campaign and its language through other official posts.“The question is: Why has there been no strong public rebuttal from the Modi government on this insult to Indians?” Ramesh said.The Congress leader also linked the controversy to earlier instances in which he accused the government of failing to defend Indian interests before the US administration. He recalled the deportation of Indians on US military aircraft in handcuffs and leg shackles and the imposition of additional US tariffs on India.“Why has our diplomatic strength become so feeble during the tenure of the Modi government, which boasts of being the 'vishwaguru', that India's interests and sovereignty are facing one blow after another?” Ramesh said.“Why is the Modi government silent? Why does the Government of India keep proving itself weak time and again?” he said.Ramesh questioned whether the government's relationship with US President Donald Trump meant that Washington could continue to target Indians while India remained silent.“Friendship is important in foreign policy, but national interest, the dignity of Indians, and India's sovereignty are paramount, and there can be no compromise on them,” he said.The controversy erupted after DHS used AI-generated imagery as part of a campaign against unlicensed commercial drivers. The advertisement showed a brown-bearded man and referred specifically to “Mr Singh”.The reference drew criticism from advocacy groups, including the Hindu American Foundation (HAF) and Sikh Coalition, which accused the US agency of racial profiling.“Singhs are Hindu, they are Sikhs, they are American and they drive. Racist, un-American, anti-Indian profiling/trolling by @DHSgov should shock our nation's collective conscience,” the HAF said on X.“This is a discriminatory post by a federal agency that is far beyond political messaging, and we welcome an investigation,” the organisation said, tagging Assistant Attorney General Harmeet K Dhillon and FBI Director Kash Patel.The Sikh Coalition said the incident showed that Sikhs continued to face profiling based on their appearance.“Twenty-five years after 9/11, Sikhs are still being targeted and profiled for how we look,” it said.“Millions of Sikhs in the United States have the last name Singh, which means lion. We remain fearless in identifying as Sikhs even when our government portrays us as enemies,” the Sikh Coalition said.Other DHS posts as part of the campaign featured characters from the Transformers franchise. One video showed Megatron negotiating the release of truck drivers Harjinder Singh, Rajinder Kumar, Bekzhan Beishekeev, Akhror Bozorov and Jasveer Singh, who the agency said were involved in road accidents and other crimes.“If you approach this nation with hostile intent, know this. We will defend ourselves. We will defend Americanism. We will defend our home,” the DHS said in a post on X.Another post featured Optimus Prime with a DHS arm patch confronting the brown-bearded man alongside the message: “Self-deport or find out”.The controversy comes amid the DHS campaign to promote its CBP Home programme, which allows eligible undocumented migrants to register their intention to leave the US voluntarily. Those opting for self-deportation can receive travel assistance and an exit bonus of USD 2,600, according to the DHS.
Article Summary: Opposition party accuses government of being 'weak' and failing to firmly defend India’s interests and the dignity of Indians abroad. Congress general secretary in-charge communications Jairam Ramesh said the advertisement was highly offensive. He said the government should have strongly rebutted what he described as racial stereotyping and ‘this level of governmental rudeness’

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday paid tributes to the victims of the 9/11 terror attacks in the United States.

Article Title: 'Festivals are inclusive': Amruta Fadnavis opposes VHP call to bar Muslims from Navratri events

Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis, his wife Amruta Fadnavis (File Photo)

NEW DELHI: Amruta Fadnavis , wife of Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis , said there was nothing wrong with Muslims participating in Navratri and other festivals, after the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) called for Muslims to be barred from the upcoming Navratri festivities, a demand endorsed by state minister Nitesh Rane.“Festivals are inclusive, and there is nothing wrong with a Muslim person attending the celebrations. Article Title: DMK MLAs bundled out as row over Vijay’s remarks rocks Tamil Nadu assembly
Article Text:
Speaker JCD Prabhakar refused to accept DMK's demand to expunge CM Vijay's remark from assembly records

CHENNAI: DMK legislators were bundled out of the Tamil Nadu assembly on Tuesday after a stormy confrontation over chief minister C Joseph Vijay’s remarks on late chief minister M Karunanidhi, former Union minister Murasoli Maran, the Sarkaria Commission and ED dossiers relating to cases pending before courts.The dramatic scenes unfolded after speaker J C D Prabhakar refused to expunge Vijay’s remarks, prompting DMK members to raise slogans and staged a sit-in protest on the well of the House. As the protesting members refused to return to their seats despite repeated appeals, the speaker ordered marshals to remove them.The confrontation began during Zero Hour when DMK whip E V Velu raised objections to Vijay’s remarks made during his reply to the demands for grants for the home department on Monday. Velu accused the CM of making baseless allegations and referring to pending cases, saying this went against the traditions of the House.Referring to the Sarkaria Commission, Velu said late chief minister M G Ramachandran was the principal complainant but later told the commission that he had “no idea whatsoever” about the complaint and that it had been drafted by a party functionary, Kannan from Salem. “At the conclusion, Sarkaria made it clear that there was no prima facie case in all the 28 allegations.Therefore, there was no provision for filing any case,” Velu said.He referred to DK leader K Veeramani and Left leaders being booked under MISA, like DMK leader M K Stalin, and said Vijay’s remarks had demeaned their democratic struggle.Ministers Aadhav Arjuna and R Nirmalkumar defended the CM, saying Vijay had referred to the Sarkaria Commission report and other publicly available documents as part of his fight against corruption. They accused the DMK of being the “root of corruption.”Former minister Govi Chezhiaan then posed three questions to the treasury benches: whether the CM could cite ED dossiers as evidence when the cases were pending before courts? whether the Sarkaria Commission could be selectively used for political gains when it had not found anyone guilty of corruption? and why Vijay had chosen to refer to late leaders such as Murasoli Maran?With no response forthcoming from either the treasury benches or the speaker, DMK intensified its protest.The situation turned chaotic after speaker Prabhakar ruled that there was “no need to expunge the CM’s remarks”. He said Vijay had merely referred to the Sarkaria Commission, whose findings had been discussed in the House earlier, and that the CM’s speech was within the rules of the assembly.The ruling triggered a fresh round of protests, with DMK MLAs raising slogans and sitting in the well, keeping the moments tense for nearly 45 minutes, starting from 9.31am and ending at about 10.11am. In between, the speaker also cautioned minister Aadhav Arjuna for his remarks that they would also match the opposition.The speaker repeatedly asked the members to return to their seats and offered to allow Velu and deputy leader of the opposition K N Nehru to speak on the issue. But the DMK members refused to relent.“I will not reverse my ruling,” Prabhakar asserted before directing marshals to remove the protesting MLAs. He cautioned Kallakurichi MLA Vasantham K Karthikeyan against approaching the Chair.Marshals entered the House at about 10.08am and physically removed several MLAs who refused to leave the well, including Kutty alias A Sudhakar of Valparai, Durai Chandrasekaran of Thiruvaiyaru and Vasantham Karthikeyan of Rishivandiyam.Later in the day, Chezhiaan moved a privilege motion against Vijay, accusing the CM of making “baseless allegations” and citing reports connected to cases pending before courts during his reply to the demands for grants for the home department.
Article Summary: Dramatic scenes unfolded after speaker J C D Prabhakar refused to expunge Vijay’s remarks. DMK members raised slogans and staged a sit-in protest on the well of the House. As the protesting members refused to return to their seats, the speaker ordered marshals to remove them.

Article Title: Delhi building collapse: SC appointed amicus curiae seeks safety audit of PGs, hostels across capital

6 killed in Satya Niketan building collapse; FIR against owner
