NEW DELHI: A Supreme Court-appointed amicus curiae on Wednesday filed a report before the top court on the building collapse in Satya Niketan and requested the apex court to direct its appointed committee to carry out inspections and safety audits of all PG accommodations, private hostels and similar student-accommodation establishments situated in and around colleges and universities across Delhi.Senior advocate Ajit Kumar Sinha, in his report, said that the Satya Niketan incident assumes significance as the locality had witnessed another building collapse in April 2022, in which two people were killed and four injured.“The present incident is also required to be viewed in the context of an earlier building collapse in Satya Niketan in April 2022, in which two persons lost their lives, and four others were injured. The recurrence of such an incident in the same locality raises serious concerns regarding the effectiveness of the existing mechanism for inspection, identification of dangerous structures, and enforcement of building bye-laws”, the amicus report said.He also noted that construction-related work was being undertaken in or around the basement and that there were reports of waterlogging in the basement immediately before the latest collapse.The amicus has sought a time-bound inspection and safety audit of PGs, private hostels and similar student-accommodation establishments around colleges and universities across Delhi, including checks on sanctioned building plans, actual construction and number of floors, basement construction and alterations, land use, structural and fire safety, ingress and egress, and dangerous or ruinous conditions.This comes after seven people were killed when a building collapsed in Satya Niketan on Sunday.Meanwhile, Municipal Corporation of Delhi also directed its executive engineers (building) across all zones to inspect structures under their jurisdiction and submit comprehensive reports by September 10, following the deadly building collapse in south Delhi's Satya Niketan, which killed seven people, officials said.Officials said the information collected during the inspections would be incorporated into an affidavit to be filed before the Delhi High Court within 10 days.The inspections and submission of reports will be personally monitored and supervised by the additional commissioners concerned in each zone, according to the order, they added.
Article Summary: A Supreme Court-appointed amicus curiae filed a report before the top court on the building collapse in Satya Niketan. He requested the apex court to direct its appointed committee to carry out inspections and safety audits of all PG accommodations, private hostels and similar student-accommodation establishments situated in and around colleges and universities.

Article Title: Qaida releases video of Osama's son who was reportedly killed in 2019
Article Text:
Osama bin Laden (File photo)

On the 25th anniversary of the Sept 11 attacks, al-Qaida's official media wing, As-Sahab, has released a propaganda video featuring the first-ever footage of Hamza bin Laden, the son and designated heir of Osama bin Laden. The video's release has drawn scrutiny from intelligence analysts, primarily because Hamza was reported to have been killed in a US counterterrorism operation along the Afghan-Pakistan border around 2019.The 50-minute-long video titled "A Quarter Century of the 11 September Raids" also features unseen images of slain AQ chief Ayman Al Zawahiri. The outfit has not acknowledged his death to date or issued its customary funeral eulogy. The video aims to propagate the ideological doctrine associated with the current outfit chief, Saif al-Adl, with the Bin Laden name aimed at recruitment.Intriguingly, the video opens not with international operations, but with historical footage from the Sept 2014 al-Qaida in the Indian Subcontinent attack on the Karachi naval dockyard. Intelligence sources noted that prioritising this regional operation underscores the influence of Pakistani terrorists within both al-Qaida's central leadership and its propaganda apparatus.Visually, the footage, they said, was meticulously staged to evoke a sense of ideological nostalgia. Hamza appears multiple times in the footage, seated against a stark, cracked mud wall, clad in a traditional white turban with an assault rifle propped beside him. "The deliberate choice of staging serves a clear dual purpose: establishing Hamza's authority as his father's successor while invoking the classic visual identity of early global jihadism," said a source.
Article Summary: The 50-minute-long video titled "A Quarter Century of the 11 September Raids" also features unseen images of slain AQ chief Ayman Al Zawahiri. Hamza appears multiple times in the footage, seated against a stark, cracked mud wall, clad in a traditional white turban.

Article Title: Upset after being fired, ex-Armyman may have stolen weapons as a form of revenge
Article Text:
The stolen Army weapons that were recovered from retired havildar

TOI





HYDERABAD: A retired havildar who had been fired from his post-retirement job in June by the Army for indiscipline, single-handedly stole 12 military grade weapons and ammunition from the Madras Regiment armoury at Bollarum on Aug 30 night. Officers said he carried the guns out of the heavily guarded cantonment on his Activa scooter.Senior police officers said on Friday that the ex-serviceman, 37-year-old Upputholla Mallesh, who was upset with his superiors after being fired, is believed to have stolen the weapons, including five assault rifles and seven pistols, as a form of revenge. However, investigators said the real motive still needs to be probed.Investigators said the case was cracked after Mallesh’s wife and father-in-law were questioned by the investigators. The wife later confronted the accused about the theft and forced him to surrender before the authorities. Mallesh also helped the police recover the weapons.was the first to report on Friday morning that the case had been solved and the weapons recovered.Speaking to reporters, DGP C V Anand said Mallesh had been arrested and the weapons recovered from an open field in Nagarkurnool district from under stacks of hay, about 185 km from Bollarum.The accused, who previously worked in the 20th battalion of the Madras Regiment had planned the theft meticulously and even conducted a recce of the armoury for two days, on Aug 28 and 29. Having worked with the Army for 16 years, he knew the topography of the area well and also understood how the armoury functioned.
Article Summary: Upputholla Mallesh, 37, was fired from his post-retirement job in June by the Army for indiscipline. He is believed to have stolen the weapons, including five assault rifles and seven pistols, as a form of revenge. Mallesh also helped the police recover the weapons.

Article Title: Saudi Arabia shuts key oil pipeline as Houthis seize strategic Red Sea island
Article Text:
The pipeline has been moving between 4 million and 5 million barrels of oil per day in recent months

Pipeline hit as Red Sea route tightens

Houthis seize strategic Red Sea island

Saudi Arabia has shut down its major East-West oil pipeline after it was attacked by drones, as the widening Iran war opened another front around one of the world’s most important energy corridors. The pipeline, which carries millions of barrels of crude across the Arabian Peninsula, was struck on Thursday in the Riyadh and Madinah regions, leaving several people injured and causing damage that is still being assessed.The Saudi Energy Ministry said Friday that the pipeline had been shut down as “a precautionary measure” after multiple attacks. The Saudi Foreign Ministry said the strikes were carried out by several drones coming from Iraq, where Iranian-backed militias operate, and that the attacks “caused human injuries and damage.”Saudi Arabia has so far held back from retaliation after Iraq’s prime minister asked Riyadh to give Baghdad time to take action against those responsible. The kingdom said it “reserves the right to take all necessary measures to protect its sovereignty, its security, its facilities,” and its inhabitants.Built in the 1980s, the roughly 1,200-kilometre East-West pipeline has become increasingly important during the Iran war because it allows Saudi Arabia to bypass the Strait of Hormuz, where tanker traffic has been severely disrupted.The pipeline runs from Saudi Arabia’s oil-producing east to Yanbu on the Red Sea coast, providing an alternative route for crude exports.The pipeline has been moving between 4 million and 5 million barrels of oil per day in recent months, equivalent to roughly 4% to 5% of global supply, according to ship-tracking companies and analysts. By early June, Saudi Arabia had more than doubled oil exports from Yanbu to more than 5 million barrels per day.An early assessment by US officials found that pumping stations located alongside the pipeline were hit. Satellite imagery showed fire and thick black smoke rising from at least one pumping station. It remained unclear how long repairs would take or whether sections of the pipeline itself had suffered damage.Saudi Arabia’s Foreign Ministry said the kingdom had chosen not to respond “at this stage” following a request from the Iraqi prime minister. Iraq condemned the attack and said it would not allow its territory or airspace to be used to launch attacks against Saudi Arabia or neighbouring countries.The Iraqi prime minister’s office also announced the dismissal of a military commander after an investigation found that the attack originated from Iraq. Two Iraqi security sources said Baghdad had additionally ordered the closure of the Shalamcheh border crossing with Iran as a precautionary measure, while a wide-scale operation was launched to track down those responsible.The pipeline attack came as Iran-backed Houthi rebels tightened their grip on the southern entrance to the Red Sea. Yemeni government sources said the Houthis had captured Perim Island, a strategically important position in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, after also taking control of the port city of Mocha.The Bab el-Mandeb has become more significant since the war disrupted the Strait of Hormuz. Before the conflict, about 20 million barrels of oil a day passed through Hormuz, representing around a fifth of global supply. With that route disrupted, Saudi Arabia increasingly relied on its East-West pipeline and Red Sea exports.Saudi crude flows through Bab el-Mandeb had already fallen sharply because of Houthi threats. Further disruption could force oil tankers to take much longer routes, increasing shipping costs and adding pressure to global energy prices, which have already surged above $100 a barrel.
Article Summary: Saudi Arabia has shut down its major East-West oil pipeline after it was attacked by drones. The pipeline, which carries millions of barrels of crude across the Arabian Peninsula, was struck on Thursday. The Saudi Foreign Ministry said the strikes were carried out by several drones coming from Iraq, where Iranian-backed militias operate.

Article Title: 44 injured, 18-year-old critically hurt after train derails in northern France
Article Text:
Transport Minister Philippe Tabarot said around 140 firefighters and emergency personnel were deployed to the scene

At least 44 people were injured, including one seriously, after a passenger train derailed in northern France on Friday evening, officials said. The train, carrying around 180 passengers, was travelling between Rouen and Caen when it went off the tracks near Cléon in Normandy, shortly before 20:00 local time.An 18-year-old woman was critically injured and airlifted to Rouen University Hospital, while 43 others reportedly suffered minor injuries. Transport Minister Philippe Tabarot said around 140 firefighters and emergency personnel were deployed to the scene. Uninjured passengers were taken to Cléon Town Hall. The cause of the derailment was not immediately known. SNCF reported significant disruption to rail services in the area and said replacement buses would be provided.
Article Summary: The train was travelling between Rouen and Caen when it went off the tracks. An 18-year-old woman was critically injured and airlifted to Rouen University Hospital. Transport Minister Philippe Tabarot said around 140 firefighters and emergency personnel were deployed to the scene.

Article Title: 'Alien terrorist': Afghan woman faces first-of-its-kind deportation over failed mass shooting in US
Article Text:
The 47-year-old woman was arrested in July

A woman in the US has been deported to Afghanistan after admitting in a rarely used federal court that she was an “alien terrorist”. The court was created three decades ago but held its first hearing only this year.The US justice department accused Nazira Haji Zada, 47, of supporting her son and son-in-law as they prepared a mass shooting inspired by the Islamic State for election day 2024. The attack never took place, and both men were arrested and later convicted on terrorism-related charges.Haji Zada, who previously lived at Fort Worth in Texas, was not charged with any crime herself. While she agreed to be removed from the United States, her lawyers argued that the proceedings had denied them access to classified evidence and violated fundamental constitutional protections.Her case was the first to be heard by the Alien Terrorist Removal Court, which Congress established in 1996 to enable the swift deportation of suspected terrorists while restricting the public disclosure of sensitive intelligence.According to court documents made public on Friday, the case was settled through a plea agreement last month. However, in a joint filing dated August 20, the Justice Department and Haji Zada’s defence agreed that she was an “alien terrorist”.The admissions she made cannot be used against her in any criminal case. The court’s chief judge approved her deportation on the same day.Attorney general Todd Blanche called the outcome a “landmark case” and “a win for national security and the rule of law”.Her public defenders, Matthew Farley and Mary Manning Petras, argued that the use of undisclosed classified evidence and the court’s unprecedented procedures had violated her due process rights.“Our client's choice to consent to removal should not be seen as an endorsement of this court's legitimacy,” they said, accusing that dragging lawful permanent residents into court but refusing to show them or their attorneys the evidence that will be used against them is a plain violation of due process.
Article Summary: Nazira Haji Zada, 47, was accused of supporting her son and son-in-law as they prepared a mass shooting inspired by the Islamic State for election day 2024. The attack never took place, and both men were arrested and later convicted on terrorism-related charges. Her case was the first to be heard by the Alien Terrorist Removal Court.

Article Title: Veteran Congress leader and socialist thinker Ratnakar Mahajan dies at 80 in Pune
Article Text:
Senior Congress leader Dr Ratnakar Mahajan passed away in Pune on Saturday





PUNE: Senior Congress leader , socialist thinker and political analyst Dr Ratnakar Mahajan died at his residence in Pune on Saturday following a brief illness, his close associates said. He was 80.Mahajan had been unwell for the past few days, according to his associates. His last rites will be performed at the Vaikunth Smashanbhoomi in Pune later on Saturday, news agency PTI reported.Mahajan hailed from Indapur taluka and moved to Pune to pursue higher education. He later became associated with several social and political movements, working on social causes through organisations including the Yuvak Kranti Dal, Rashtra Seva Dal and Bharat Jodo Abhiyan, besides student movements.After joining the Congress , Mahajan served as the spokesperson of the party's Maharashtra unit. He also served as the editor of*'Shidori' magazine.Mahajan was known for his engagement with socialist thought, political analysis and social movements over the course of his public life.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Mahajan had been unwell for the past few days, according to his associates. His last rites will be performed at the Vaikunth Smashanbhoomi in Pune later on Saturday. Mahajan hailed from Indapur taluka and moved to Pune to pursue higher education.

Article Title: Gurgaon waterlogging has direct bearing on human rights: HHRC
Article Text:
A school bus stranded on a flooded Subhas Chowk stretch on Aug 26

TOI





GURGAON: Recurring waterlogging in Gurgaon is not merely a civic inconvenience but has a direct bearing on citizens’ human rights, Haryana Human Rights Commission (HHRC) has observed. Taking suo motu cognisance of TOI reports, the commission ordered govt agencies to conduct a comprehensive audit of the city’s drainage and civic infrastructure.In an order published Friday, the commission noted that the problem appeared to have persisted over several years and, therefore, could not be attributed to one wet spell. Such repeated disruption of roads, schools, emergency services, water supply and everyday mobility during heavy rain could not be treated as an “unavoidable feature of urban life”, it said.Drainage was a “basic and essential prerequisite” of planned urban development, HHRC said, linking its failure with Article 21 of Constitution, which guarantees the right to life and personal liberty, including living with dignity in conditions conducive to health and safety. It also referred to the constitutional obligations related to public health and environmental protection.The HHRC full bench, comprising Justice (retd) Lalit Batra, judicial member Kuldeep Jain and member Deep Bhatia, stopped short of holding any agency responsible at this stage.It said persistent failure of essential civic infrastructure, “if attributable to neglect, inadequate planning, failure of maintenance or failure to take reasonable preventive measures”, may have a direct bearing on human rights. The proceedings, it said, would ascertain the facts, determine responsibility, and secure preventive and remedial measures.The commission pointed to the ordeal of school students stranded in buses, parents wading through flooded roads, and the difficulties in getting information about children’s safety. It also referred to reports of commuters taking disproportionately long to cover short distances and the disruption to ambulances and essential services during the Aug 24 downpour, reported byThe panel stressed that Gurgaon’s civic infrastructure must match the scale and density of its population and economic activity.The commission ordered GMDA, the municipal corporation, Haryana Shehri Vikas Pradhikaran, PWD, the public health engineering department, the irrigation and water resources department, DHBVN, town planning authorities and the district administration to conduct a technical audit of Gurgaon’s drainage and associated infrastructure.The audit will have to identify the capacity of the existing storm-water network, natural drains and watercourses, chronic waterlogging points (including the 99 locations flagged by authorities), causes of water accumulation, condition of drains and pumping stations, possible interconnection of sewage and storm-water systems, vulnerable underground utilities, and road-level and drainage deficiencies.HHRC further ordered GIS-based mapping of natural and engineered drainage channels and identification of encroachments or obstructions affecting natural drainage. It asked the authorities concerned to assess whether the existing system could cope with present and projected rainfall and future urbanisation.Separately, the commission sought a report on implementation of the SOP on school transport. It called for real-time tracking of school buses; communication between schools, parents, police and the administration; designated safe holding points, and restrictions on school buses entering identified high-risk waterlogging locations during extreme rainfall.It also directed authorities to identify emergency corridors for ambulances, fire services and police, and ordered a vulnerability assessment of roads, culverts, underpasses and underground utilities, particularly around the cave-in reported near IFFCO Chowk.Agencies will have to provide details of drainage deficiencies reported during the last five years, remedial measures sanctioned and the status of their implementation. They must also furnish details of pre-monsoon desilting, pumping capacity, deployment during the Aug 24 rainfall, response times, and the time taken to clear waterlogging at major locations.The commission suggested an independent technical assessment be undertaken by an IIT, NIT or another reputable hydrological/urban infrastructure institution, covering the whole Gurgaon drainage basin rather than examining individual waterlogging spots in isolation.
Article Summary: Recurring waterlogging in Gurgaon is not merely a civic inconvenience but has a direct bearing on citizens’ human rights, Haryana Human Rights Commission (HHRC) has observed. Taking suo motu cognisance of TOI reports, the commission ordered govt agencies to conduct a comprehensive audit of the city’s drainage and civic infrastructure.

Article Title: LeT founder Hafiz Saeed in Pakistan, aiding Kashmir terrorists: NIA; Jammu court issues non-bailable warrant
Article Text:
India's most-wanted terrorist Hafiz Saeed is reportedly in Pakistan, the NIA informed a Jammu court

Hafiz Saeed terror case: How probe led to LeT founder

Jammu court issues second NBW against Hafiz Saeed

Hafiz Saeed's link to Pahalgam terror attack





JAMMU: Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) founder and India's most-wanted terrorist Hafiz Saeed is currently in Pakistan, the National Investigation Agency ( NIA ) told a Special Court in Jammu, which issued a second non-bailable warrant (NBW) against him in two months in connection with a terror case involving the alleged supply of weapons, funds and directions to terror groups operating in Jammu and Kashmir.The NIA moved an application seeking an NBW against Saeed under Section 75 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). The LeT founder, a designated terrorist and resident of Sargodha in Pakistan's Punjab province, has been described as an "absconding accused" in the case.The case relates to the arrest of Mohammad Naqeeb Bhat during a check at Pandach on the outskirts of Srinagar earlier this year. A China-made grenade and 15 live rounds were recovered from Bhat, a resident of Batpora.Bhat was subsequently booked at Zakoora Police Station under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), Arms Act and Explosive Substances Act.Further investigation into the case led to the busting of a terror network and the arrest of several more terrorists allegedly associated with LeT and its offshoot, The Resistance Front (TRF), along with two Pakistani nationals.According to the NIA, Saeed's alleged involvement emerged during the investigation.The agency said the arrested Pakistani terrorists were allegedly associated with him."Saeed is operating from Pakistan and providing weapons, money and directions to terrorists operating in the Kashmir Valley. The information is gathered that the said terrorist at present is in Pakistan and deliberately evading his arrest to escape the clutches of law," the NIA told the court.After hearing the NIA's submissions, Special Judge under the NIA Act Prem Sagar on September 8 observed that Saeed's involvement had emerged during the investigation and that he was "allegedly involved in terrorism."The court also noted that Saeed was at large and that the investigating agency had been unable to secure his attendance "in the ordinary manner". It subsequently issued a general non-bailable warrant against him.The latest warrant is the second NBW issued against Saeed by the Special NIA Court in Jammu in two months.Earlier, on July 8, the same court had issued an NBW against Saeed in connection with the Pahalgam terror attack in April, in which 25 tourists and a local resident were killed.Saeed is the founder of the proscribed LeT and a designated terrorist.The latest proceedings relate to the separate terror case involving the alleged supply of weapons, funds and directions to terror operatives in the Union Territory.(With PTI inputs)
Article Summary: India's most-wanted terrorist Hafiz Saeed is reportedly in Pakistan, the NIA informed a Jammu court. The LeT founder, a designated terrorist, has been described as an "absconding accused" in the case. The case relates to the arrest of Mohammad Naqeeb Bhat during a check at Pandach.

Article Title: Rape convict ex-MP Prajwal Revanna's smuggled jail phone contained multiple pornographic videos: Police
Article Text:
During the inspection, a prohibited mobile phone, SIM card, charger and notebook were found in a cell.





BENGALURU: Multiple pornographic videos were found on a mobile phone seized from jailed former Janata Dal (Secular) MP Prajwal Revanna , police sources told TOI on Saturday.Revanna, the former Hassan MP who is currently serving a sentence after being convicted in a sexual assault case, allegedly received a mobile phone, SIM card, charger and pen drive in a coordinated smuggling operation involving five others, including a jail staffer, police said.All five people have been arrested in connection with the case, police said.Investigators said Revanna allegedly paid Rs 70,000 to have the mobile phone smuggled into the prison and another Rs 30,000 for the SIM card.Jail warden Prakash Gawade allegedly handed the phone to Revanna personally. Undertrial prisoner Mohammed Tausif, who is accused in the DJ Halli case, allegedly concealed the SIM card in his mouth and passed it to Revanna, police said.Gawade allegedly handed over the charger and pen drive to Revanna during subsequent visits, investigators said. The jail staffer had previously been arrested and suspended on charges of allegedly smuggling ganja into the prison.In August, Central Crime Branch officers raided Revanna’s barrack and seized the mobile phone, SIM card, charger and pen drive. An FIR was subsequently registered against Revanna and his co-inmate Pratap Rai.Rai, however, denied any involvement, saying Revanna had been using the mobile phone even before Rai joined him in the barrack.“While Naveen and Siddiqui arranged the phone and the Sim, Manjunath connected these men with Prajwal and Gawde. The four private persons and Prajwal said that besides paying money for mobile and Sim, they paid Rs 1 lakh (Rs 70,000 for mobile and Rs 30,000 for Sim) to Gawde,” an investigating officer told TOI.
Article Summary: Multiple pornographic videos were found on a mobile phone seized from jailed former Janata Dal (Secular) MP Prajwal Revanna. Revanna allegedly paid Rs 70,000 to have the mobile phone smuggled into the prison and another Rs 30,000 for the SIM card. Five people have been arrested in connection with the case.

Article Title: Applied, invested, still outside: Pakistan is still waiting at the Brics door
Article Text:
Pakistan seeks Brics entry for economic relief, but India’s veto keeps the door shut.

Islamabad confirmed its application in 2023

Pakistan seeks economic support through Brics

India’s opposition keeps Pakistan outside

Pakistan’s attempt to join Brics remains unresolved as leaders of the grouping gather in New Delhi for the 18th summit. Islamabad formally applied for membership in 2023, but India’s opposition has kept it outside the bloc.Brics originally comprised Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa. The grouping expanded in 2024 with the inclusion of Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the United Arab Emirates, becoming known as Brics+. Saudi Arabia and Argentina were also invited during the expansion process, although Argentina later declined to join.Pakistan publicly confirmed its Brics membership application in 2023, when the grouping was preparing for a major expansion under Russia’s presidency.Foreign Office spokesperson Mumtaz Zahra Baloch announced the move during her weekly press briefing."Yes, I can confirm that Pakistan has made a formal request to join Brics, which we believe is an important grouping of developing countries," Baloch said.She said Pakistan had friendly relations with most Brics members and the countries invited to join the bloc. Baloch also highlighted Islamabad’s support for multilateralism and its participation in international organisations working for global peace and development."We believe that by joining Brics, Pakistan can play an important role in furthering international cooperation and revitalising inclusive multilateralism.Baloch’s statement came as the grouping prepared to admit Argentina, Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates. The new members were expected to formally join during the 2024 summit in Russia.Pakistan is among 29 countries that have applied to join Brics. Its bid is largely linked to its economic difficulties and the need to find new sources of funding.According to the Pakistan Economic Survey, the country’s GDP growth stood at 3.70 per cent. A report by Nikkei Asia said Pakistan had purchased a $580 million stake in the Brics-backed New Development Bank. The move was aimed at widening Islamabad’s financing options and reducing its dependence on the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund.Despite its application and the bloc’s expansion, Pakistan has not secured membership. New Delhi’s veto power within Brics has effectively blocked Islamabad’s entry.Pakistan’s bid also comes against the backdrop of wider regional tensions and its strained relations with India. While Islamabad has sought to present membership as part of its economic and diplomatic strategy, India’s opposition remains the main obstacle.During the 2023 briefing, Baloch also called for action by Afghan authorities against terrorist groups operating from Afghanistan. She reiterated Pakistan’s support for an international peace conference on the Palestinian issue and the implementation of United Nations resolutions supporting a two-state solution.
Article Summary: Pakistan formally applied for membership in 2023. India’s opposition has kept it outside the bloc. Brics originally comprised Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa. The grouping expanded in 2024 with the inclusion of Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the United Arab Emirates.

Article Title: 'Only tea was good': Near Jantar Mantar, Sonam Wangchuk appeals for support to Ladakh’s fight for democracy
Article Text:
Sonam Wangchuk





SRINAGAR: Leh Apex Body (LAB) member and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk early Saturday appealed to people across the country to support Ladakh’s fight for democracy, saying the Centre had failed to give Ladakhi leaders an assurance at the September 9 meeting that major decisions concerning land allotment and local governance would not be taken by the current administration until a democratic government was formed in the Union Territory. The founder of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), Abhijeet Dipke, supported Wangchuk, stating, “Stand with Ladakh!”“Hello friends, cockroaches, how are you? I am in Delhi and right next to the place where we spent weeks with you all, starving, yes, Jantar Mantar. But don’t worry. I am not here for any protest or fast. We came here from Ladakh for a meeting with the Home Ministry for a dialogue. The meeting has been going on for the preservation of the culture, nature and land of Ladakh, and this meeting was also part of it,” Wangchuk said in a message posted on social media early Saturday.Wangchuk shared a video of famous comedian Jaspal Bhatti, saying the meeting resulted in no new steps except fixing the date for the next meeting. “Only tea was good in the meeting, otherwise no new decision was made,” he said. He said decisions already taken, including the creation of a democratic structure in Ladakh under an assembly, were repeated. But he said the government did not provide any assurance that the process of the proposed Assembly would not be undermined by major decisions taken by the local administration and the office of the lieutenant governor in Ladakh.“We had only expected a small, legitimate assurance from the government that until a democratic structure is established in Ladakh, the UT administration should not take any major decisions that would change the face of Ladakh, whether it is land allotment or local governance. No major changes should be brought in these areas and it should be done in coordination with the democratic structure.”Wangchuk said if they get an assurance from the government within a week on the issue, they will celebrate the padyatra from September 19 to September 24 as “a memorial padyatra of the martyrs who sacrificed their lives for Ladakh.”“Otherwise, we will make it a big demonstration on behalf of the people of the entire country that justice should be done to Ladakh,” he said, adding that, as in every other state in the country, major decisions should be left to the people.On September 9, the Leh Apex Body and Kargil Democratic Alliance, the two organisations negotiating with the Union government for administrative autonomy for Ladakh, held talks with the MHA’s subcommittee in Delhi.After the talks, chief secretary of Ladakh Ashish Kundra said the Centre had agreed to have a legislative body under Article 371 in the region, but it would require a constitutional amendment with a two-thirds majority in Parliament.“There was a discussion on whether there would be direct or indirect elections of the UT legislative body through the Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils. Representatives of LAB and KDA said elections should be direct and a consensus was reached on this issue,” Kundra said at a press conference in Leh. “The question that remains to be answered concerns the relationship between the LAHDCs and the UT-level body. What powers will be vested in LAHDCs and what will be the jurisdiction of the UT-level body?”The chief secretary said the Centre had handed the Ladakh groups a list of eight to 10 questions to which they did not have immediate answers. “They were requested to think about those, consult the public and tell us what they think, so that we can move towards a draft by taking these issues forward at the next meeting in October,” he said.The chief secretary said the Centre did not want to impose any administrative model that was not acceptable to the people. “We want to move forward only after discussion with everyone. When in good faith and in the interest of everyone, everything is moving forward, it is the responsibility of the leadership here to create an environment of positivity among people, to give them hope that things are moving forward.”In a joint statement after the meeting, the LAB and KDA said the meeting furthered the “in-principle understanding” reached during talks on May 22 and July 3 on Ladakh’s demands, including constitutional safeguards through special provisions under Article 371. They said the MHA stopped short of guaranteeing powers across the board under Lists II and III of the Seventh Schedule, including law and order.The groups, however, expressed concern about “developments taking place with respect to formation of new districts, creation of hill councils of each of the new districts, and other” major irreversible changes being made before an elected body at the Union Territory level.LAB and KDA said they unanimously opposed what they called “irreversible changes” being made to the administrative and political setup of Ladakh before the UT-level body was formed.Ladakhi representatives have been in talks with the MHA since 2023 for safeguards covering land, jobs, culture and the environment. The MHA set up the committee on January 2, 2023, but the process stalled after four people were killed and more than 80 injured in alleged police firing on protesters demanding statehood in Leh in September last year.Wangchuk was accused of inciting the protesters. He was arrested, charged under the NSA and kept in Jodhpur jail. The Centre revoked his NSA detention in March this year. After his release, Wangchuk participated in the May 22 talks with the Centre. He was also one of the LAB representatives at the September 9 talks.
Article Summary: Leh Apex Body member and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk appealed to people across the country to support Ladakh’s fight for democracy. He said the Centre had failed to give Ladakhi leaders an assurance that major decisions would not be taken by the current administration until a democratic government was formed in the Union Territory.

Article Title: CM Vijay skips VIP gate at Chennai airport after advisor denied special entry for London trip
Article Text:
For his upcoming London trip, Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay has decided to enter through the regular passenger terminal, defying VIP access.





CHENNAI: Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay is set to skip the VIP entry into Chennai airport via Gate 6 and will enter through the regular T2 international terminal like other passengers to fly to London, after the Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS) denied entry to his advisor Vishnu Reddy, who is accompanying the CM on his maiden overseas visit to woo investments, citing security reasons.Airport sources said only the President and Prime Minister are eligible for ceremonial entry into the airport, while the facility is extended to the chief minister and governor of the particular state on special request.While the chief minister's office made a request for special entry for the chief minister on Thursday, BCAS accepted it but said that persons accompanying the VIP should enter through the regular international terminal as per protocol.However, the chief minister reportedly refused to use the VIP gate only for himself and decided to enter the airport like other international passengers.After receiving the information, airport authorities made arrangements to usher in the guests through Gate No. D9, which is used only for emergencies. A heavy posse of police personnel has also been deployed at Chennai airport to avoid crowding at the terminal.
Article Summary: Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay is set to skip the VIP entry into Chennai airport via Gate 6. He will enter through the regular T2 international terminal like other passengers to fly to London. The Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS) denied entry to his advisor Vishnu Reddy, citing security reasons.

Article Title: Delhi man, 22, stabbed 17 times near school over suspected affair
Article Text:
A 22-year-old man died after being stabbed seventeen times in east Delhi's Mandawali area.





NEW DELHI: A 22-year-old man was stabbed 17 times and killed after an altercation with two men near a school in east Delhi’s Mandawali on Thursday evening, with police suspecting that the accused believed the victim was having an affair with his sister.A PCR call about the stabbing was received at 7:54pm, following which police reached near Gyan Vatika School and rushed the injured man, identified as Vansh Dedha, to Max Hospital. He was declared brought dead. Doctors found 17 stab injuries on his body.Preliminary inquiry revealed that Dedha had an altercation with Keshav Kumar, 22, a resident of Karawal Nagar, and his associate. Police suspect Kumar attacked Dedha after believing that he was having an affair with his sister. Kumar and his associate allegedly chased Dedha and repeatedly stabbed him with a sharp-edged weapon near the school before fleeing the spot.A murder case was registered at Mandawali police station and Kumar was arrested during the investigation. Police have also identified the second accused and are conducting raids to apprehend him.The knife allegedly used in the murder and the clothes worn during the incident have been recovered, while the motorcycle allegedly used by the accused has also been taken into police possession.CCTV footage from the area and technical surveillance are being examined to establish the sequence of events. Further investigation is underway.
Article Summary: A 22-year-old man was stabbed 17 times and killed after an altercation with two men near a school in east Delhi’s Mandawali on Thursday evening. Police suspect that the accused believed the victim was having an affair with his sister.

Article Title: ‘Enough is enough’: Bombay HC seeks names of ward officers responsible for garbage on streets
Article Text:
The Bombay High Court ordered the BMC to identify accountable officers for street garbage





MUMBAI: The Bombay high court on Thursday directed the BMC to submit names of ward officers and officers on field responsible for maintaining hygiene and cleanliness, who can be held accountable for garbage dumped on public streets and open spaces.“Enough is enough. The moment we get a complaint, we’ll hold the particular officer responsible and ensure he is not there in public service,’’ said Justices Girish Kulkarni and Neela Gokhale while hearing a petition by Kannamwar Nagar CHS regarding odour from Kanjurmarg dumping ground.In recent hearings, HC flagged total non-compliance by BMC in clearing trash, waste, litter on public streets. The judges said “ward officers are not functioning properly.” Referring to a photograph, Justice Kulkarni told senior advocate Anil Sakhare, for BMC, “This is Dadar. We’ll provide you with entire Mumbai (photographs), if your commissioner is not aware about it.”The judges said it appears that BMC’s assurances “were paper assurances.” “There is no alternative but to direct the municipal commissioner to put the house in order and fix accountability” on officers who are not taking action to prevent dumping of waste on public streets.They directed an SOP to be placed at the next hearing.They also said BMC will have to strictly implement Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, that casts duties on urban local bodies. “We always want Bombay (sic) corporation to be a model corporation. It is not happening… Segregation is going to have more importance in the coming times…festival times. Otherwise it will be chaotic,’’ said Justice Kulkarni. The judges also said, “the problem is there is a mental block with all citizens” and “wherever there is open space, streets, they dump waste. ”They directed expeditious appointment of a task force for implementing the Rules. Citing the example of Singapore, which imposes heavy fines on offenders, they said the state govt must come out with a “uniform policy.”Adjourning the hearing to Oct 7, the judges said BMC must issue “public sensitive” advertisements in newspapers and TV and also encourage social influencers to give messages to citizens not to throw garbage on public streets. “A sense of belonging of citizens needs to be inculcated,’’ said Justice Gokhale.
Article Summary: HC flagged total non-compliance by BMC in clearing trash, waste, litter on public streets. Justices Girish Kulkarni and Neela Gokhale said “ward officers are not functioning properly’ They also said BMC will have to strictly implement Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026.

Article Title: Watch: RTC bus swerves to avoid wrong-way car, ploughs into petrol bunk
Article Text:
Image Credit: X





HYDERABAD: A bus driver’s attempt to avoid a car that allegedly entered a service road from the wrong direction resulted in an RTC bus crashing into a petrol bunk at Batasingaram in Abdullapurmet.No injuries were reported in the incident, a video of which has since gone viral on social media.According to Abdullapurmet police, a case was registered against the RTC bus driver based on a complaint lodged by the petrol bunk manager, alleging damage to two cars and a fixed installation on the premises.Police said two cars were waiting to refuel when the bus, travelling along the service road, suddenly veered into the petrol bunk and collided with the vehicles and an installation. Bunk employees ran to safety after noticing the bus approaching at high speed. The bus eventually came to a halt inside the premises.However, an examination of CCTV footage revealed that a parked truck on the service road and a car that allegedly entered from the wrong direction contributed to the incident. Police said the bus driver’s view was obstructed by the parked truck, and he swerved left to avoid colliding with the car that suddenly appeared in front of him.Despite the evasive manoeuvre, the bus entered the petrol bunk and damaged two cars before coming to a stop. Police are investigating the incident.
Article Summary: An RTC bus crashed into a petrol bunk at Batasingaram in Abdullapurmet. No injuries were reported in the incident, a video of which has since gone viral on social media. A case has been registered against the bus driver. Police are investigating the incident.

Article Title: 20 coded messages of Akbar, Noor Jahan & Shah Jahan surface in Madhya Pradesh's Datia
Article Text:
Twenty cryptic Persian messages surfaced in Datia, Madhya Pradesh





BHOPAL: Akbar sends a blessing. Noor Jahan offers reassurance. Shah Jahan pines for a beloved. Their words travel not by horse or herald, but by pigeon — tucked into tiny tubes tied to birds’ legs, more than three centuries ago.Twenty cryptic Persian messages, each barely four square inches, have surfaced in a private collection in Madhya Pradesh’s Datia, close to the UP border about 360 km north of Bhopal. No names. No signatures. Just symbols, texts and clues to a secretive Mughal world.The messages were found in Datia resident Radha Vallabh Mishra’s collection during a recent Gyan Bharatam Mission survey by archaeologist Wasim Khan, associated with the state directorate of archaeology, archives and museums. Some are believed to have been sent directly by Akbar, Noor Jahan and Shah Jahan.Mishra, who has collected old books and rare objects for more than five decades, acquired them about 40 years ago from an antique seller in Agra for around Rs 200. He began connecting them to the Mughal period from their paper, motifs, symbols, the name “Chandra Bhan” and Hijri dates on some pages.Chandra Bhan, sometimes Chandra Bhan Brahman, was a Punjabi poet of Persian who served as secretary to Shah Jahan.Impressed by his Persian literature, calligraphy and poetry, the emperor entrusted him with maintaining his personal diary. His “Chahar Chaman” chronicles Shah Jahan’s rule.Written in coded Persian Ramz, messages were examined by Persian-language experts Noor Ishtiyaq of archaeology and museums directorate and Urdu poets Wajahat Shah and Latif Ahmad.Instead of royal names, they found three golden symbols — a square, candle and rose — associated with Akbar, Noor Jahan and Shah Jahan respectively. “These messages were placed inside tiny tubes tied to pigeons’ legs,” Khan said. Who received them remains a mystery.Pigeon post was no flight of fancy at Mughal court and the find dovetails with Abul Fazl’s “Ain-i-Akbari”, which records Akbar’s passion for pigeon-flying, or ishqbazi, and describes an aviary with more than 20,000 birds, including 500 select pigeons. It identifies Raṭh as a pigeon trained chiefly to carry letters.One message attributed to Shah Jahan dwells on a beloved’s beauty, down to a tiny mole on her face, before turning wistful — a dream surviving in the heart despite changing times. Noor Jahan’s is intimate and reassuring: “The hour has arrived; there is no need to worry; happiness, fulfilment and refuge await.” Akbar’s reads like a blessing, invoking grace, generosity and greatness and imagining life as a garden blooming through countless springs.But experts said what reads like poetry may conceal something else. In Ramz, a rose may not be a rose, and a blessing may carry a message hidden in plain sight. “Cryptography and communication have been a historic need. These letters are the evidence of our evolution,” said archaeology commissioner Madan Kumar Nagargoje. Four centuries later, pigeons are long gone. Their secrets have just landed.
Article Summary: Twenty cryptic Persian messages, each barely four square inches, have surfaced in a private collection in Madhya Pradesh’s Datia. Some are believed to have been sent directly by Akbar, Noor Jahan and Shah Jahan. The messages were placed inside tiny tubes tied to pigeons’ legs.

Article Title: Married for 10 days, couple found dead in Lucknow guest house
Article Text:
The couple had arrived from Hardoi and had been staying in a guest house in Lucknow since Aug 23.





LUCKNOW: A 22-year-old man and a 19-year-old woman were found dead in a guest house room in Chinhat area on Wednesday night. Police said they hanged themselves from a ceiling fan hook using a dupatta. Police also recovered a suicide note from the woman’s bag.The couple had arrived from Hardoi and had been staying in a guest house in Lucknow since Aug 23. They had married on Aug 21 and the man worked at a medical store.The bodies were brought down from the hanging point and sent to RMLIMS for post-mortem. Police have begun an investigation to determine the circumstances surrounding their deaths.A search of the guest house room led to the recovery of a bag, a keypad mobile phone and its charger, along with routine personal-use items, including soap, oil, a toothbrush and beauty products.Sources in the police said that the suicide note recovered from the woman’s bag stated that nobody should harass their families now and they together decided to take the extreme step.
Article Summary: The couple had arrived from Hardoi and had been staying in a guest house in Lucknow since Aug 23. They had married on Aug 21 and the man worked at a medical store. Police have begun an investigation to determine the circumstances surrounding their deaths.

Article Title: Thousands in Texas were left without internet and TV after outage; Iranian hackers say we did it; AT&T says: No, we ...
Article Text:
AT&T outage reports reached nearly 6,000

What AT&T says

Hackers warn of more attacks

AT&T outage reports reached nearly 6,000

Thousands of users in Texas were left without internet, TV and phone services after an AT&T outage on Monday, September 7. An Iranian-linked hacking group later claimed responsibility for the disruption. The group, APT IRAN, said on Telegram that it had attacked telecommunications and other critical infrastructure in Texas. It also claimed responsibility for disrupting an unnamed water utility in the state. The claim was first reported by Threat Beat, a publication associated with the McCrary Institute for Cyber and Critical Infrastructure Security at Auburn University.According to Threat Beat, APT IRAN is closely linked to CyberAv3ngers, a group affiliated with Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. APT IRAN has previously claimed attacks against water systems in several US states. The group said earlier attacks in late July targeted water systems in Minnesota, Michigan, Georgia, New Jersey, South Dakota and Arkansas. It then said those attacks were intended to warn about its ability to target critical US infrastructure.AT&T initially said the outage was linked to fiber equipment and cable issues. In an updated statement, the company rejected the hacking group's claim.“We have no evidence to support that claim. Our assessment indicates that attempted cable theft led to the outage. Internet service across Dallas and surrounding areas is operating normally, and we continue to monitor our network and review relevant information,” AT&T said.The company said internet service in Dallas and nearby areas had returned to normal.On August 30, the group claimed it would target more critical infrastructure. According to Threat Beat, APT IRAN said:"We had previously warned that anyone who encroaches on this soil and threatens our beloved Iran will pay for this mistake with their lives," The group also referred to earlier warnings involving Minnesota and said:"You ignored our warnings, and we in Minnesota warned you again. You ignored them again; but this time we will sew the lips and mouths of the American people together."The AT&T outage was first reported Monday, September 7 morning. According to Downdetector data cited by WFAA, customer reports began rising at about 2:18 a.m. A larger increase was recorded from around 10:30 a.m. Reports reached a peak of 5,990 shortly before 3 p.m. The number of reports then dropped quickly, with the outage mostly resolved by around 6 p.m.The outage affected internet, TV and phone services for some customers.
Article Summary: AT&T outage affects internet, TV and phone services for some customers. Iranian- linked hacking group claims responsibility for disruption. APT IRAN has previously claimed attacks against water systems in several US states. AT&T initially said the outage was linked to fiber equipment and cable issues.

Article Title: Hazaribag man drowns while fishing in lake
Article Text:
Hazaribag:





A man drowned in a lake of Hazaribag city while fishing, police said on Monday. The deceased was identified as Mohammad Kalim (50), a resident of Sardar Chowk Mohalla. Officer in-charge of the Lohsighna police station Rohit Kerketta said, “Family members of the deceased told police that he had left home on Sunday morning as usual to catch fish in the lake but did not return till late in the night. They began a search and found his fishing gear and a tiffin box on the bank of the lake. His body was later found floating in the lake. An investigation is under way to ascertain the circumstances leading to the death.”
Article Summary: The deceased was identified as Mohammad Kalim (50), a resident of Sardar Chowk Mohalla. Family members of the deceased told police that he had left home on Sunday morning as usual to catch fish in the lake. Article Title: Brics restrictions keep Delhi roads clear, traffic smooth
Article Text:
An unusual looking ITO crossing during peak hours Friday; traffic was halted briefly for VIP movement at Mother Teresa Crescent (L)





NEW DELHI: It was a Friday without its usual rush. As Day 1 of the traffic restrictions for Brics Summit kicked in, Delhi’s roads were mostly clear, with some congestion reported on several stretches. Schools and govt offices being shut appeared to have helped keep the usual rush in check.People who couldn’t avoid commuting got a better response to their traffic queries. Instead of the usual “contact your TI” response or a blanket advisory, traffic police addressed individual queries with route-specific information.A commuter from Greater Noida asked about reaching Terminal 3 for a flight with check-in at 12.10am on Sept 12 and whether DND Flyway would remain open.There are no restrictions for commute in the night, he was told. Another person asked how to reach Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station from Rajouri Garden by taxi, as senior citizen parents were travelling around 1pm.Traffic police suggested a route via Naraina, Dhaula Kuan, Ring Road, AIIMS, Lajpat Nagar and Ashram, while warning that temporary stoppages could occur due to VIP movement.Other queries were more straightforward. A commuter was informed that the Delhi-Noida route via Kalindi Kunj would remain open for private vehicles.Another asked about the Barapullah elevated road between Akshardham and AIIMS around 10am on Saturday and was told it would remain open, with a reminder to check the latest advisory before travelling.The responses on social media were matched by advance signage on the roads. For instance, at ITO, a board warned motorists about the W-point restriction on Mathura Road towards Bharat Mandapam, allowing them to change their route before reaching the restricted stretch.Restrictions came into force around 2pm on several roads, including Sardar Patel Marg, Mother Teresa Crescent, Teen Murti Marg, Akbar Road, Tees January Marg, Mathura Road, Moti Lal Nehru Marg, Dr Zakir Hussain Marg, Barakhamba Road, Tolstoy Marg, Janpath and Ashoka Road.For most commuters, the first day was relatively uneventful. Anuja, who travelled to New Delhi Railway Station, said she left two hours early. “Our driver said there were diversions, but there was no congestion,” she said.Another commuter said a journey to the airport that normally takes around 45 minutes took just 14 minutes Friday, with offices shut and restrictions in place.Sources attributed the relatively smooth movement partly to lower traffic volumes, with Delhi govt offices and schools shut, reducing the usual rush-hour load on the roads.The lighter traffic, however, also triggered some criticism online, with questions over whether the quiet roads were the result of putting much of the city’s normal routine on hold. One person questioned whether the empty roads were created simply by the restrictions.Another post argued that with schools shut, govt offices closed and several roads restricted, normal life had effectively been disrupted to allow visiting dignitaries to move through a largely sanitised capital.The post acknowledged that security for international guests was necessary, but questioned whether putting the city’s routine on hold was the right way to manage it.While traffic police advises everyone to leave early till Sunday, commuters are also requested to contact helpline 1095 or 011-25844444, and check @dtptraffic for the latest advisory.
Article Summary: Traffic police addressed individual queries with route-specific information. Schools and govt offices being shut appeared to have helped keep the usual rush in check. The lighter traffic triggered some criticism online, with questions over whether the quiet roads were the result of putting much of the city’s normal routine on hold.
